utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in court. Mr. Registrar, become to you, too, and may you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. And may we please have the appearances for today starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May -- may I interrupt you, Madam Vidovic. We are getting no interpretation through the English channel. Can I find out from the interpreters. Do we have any problem?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Are you hear us now? Can you hear the interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can hear you now. Thank you very much, ma'am. Madam Vidovic, would you please start all over again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to my learned friends from the Prosecution, to everyone in and around the courtroom. On behalf of General Delic, Vasvija Vidovic with case manager Lana Deljkic, legal assistant Sabina Dzubur, assisted today with legal assistants OKO by Ms. Nina Kisic from the state court of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Awad. Mr. Awad, yesterday before you started your testimony you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. I just remind you that you are still bound by that declaration today to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay? Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I resume, I would like to indicate on the record that following the adjournment yesterday, we did meet with Madam Vidovic for the Defence and attempted to review the tape that was played yesterday. Unfortunately, the Arabic part of the tape was not really audible to the extent that it would be helpful or useful, and so both parties following the review of that tape have decided that we will not be returning to that issue. I just wanted to indicate that because we -- we had discussed the possibility of that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Do you confirm, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I'd like to now turn our attention to 1995. Can you tell us, sir, whether the El Mujahedin Detachment was involved in any combat operations in 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me before answering this question to ask for protection of the Trial Chamber. Yesterday, before the beginning of the proceedings, I made the solemn declaration that I would speak the truth, and I said at the same time that I have come here to testify as a former member of the El Mujahedin, but certainly not as the president of any kind of association. Yesterday, in the news programme, the programme 1, she almost jumped out of the screen, said, "Ajman Awad, president of the association that rallies people of Afro-Asian origin is testifying in this case." Somebody wishes intentionally to undermine the prestige I enjoy among the Bosnian people, and I am asking for protection. I'm coming here in my own name as a citizen, as an individual. You can read my statement when -- in which I never mention that I was president of the association. So I'm asking the Trial Chamber to protect me from the media, that they should report correctly. As for the detachment itself, it took part in three main operations carried out during the summer of 1995 in the territory of Zavidovici-Wadnic [as interpreted] theatre -- Zavidovici-Vozuca theatre of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We hear your request, Mr. Awad, and the Court would like to place on record that at no stage has Mr. Awad stated that he was president of any association, neither was it ever mentioned at any stage in court yesterday, and any news reports that suggest that he was president or is president of any association is incorrect, and we ask those responsible for the incorrect reporting, if it is at all possible, to make the necessary corrections. If there are any people from the media in the gallery, if they still hope to -- to get the cooperation of the Court as was being requested yesterday time and again between -- by the media, we ask them also to show that cooperation by making sure that they report correctly. Okay. Let the record show that. Thank you very much, Mr. Awad. You may proceed and answer the question. You were busy answering the question that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And thank you to the Trial Chamber also for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, you told us there were three main operations in 1995. Can you please tell us the time periods --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. He was mentioning the areas where it took place. I just wanted to a note of those areas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you -- can you repeat the areas where these three operations took place in 1995.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the Zavidovici-Vozuca battlefield. Zavidovici and Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, can you tell us, please, the time periods in 1995 during which these three operations took place?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a correction, please. My surname is Awad, not Ajwad. I have to correct you a little. The operations were carried out in the month of May, in July, and in September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's focus, first, Mr. Awad, on May 1995. Can you tell us, sir, about the direction, if any, the detachment received with respect to those operations?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of 1994, when the detachment received orders to move from the Teslic battlefield to Zavidovici-Vozuca battlefield, this order remained in force until the execution of the assignment. So what we were saying yesterday, that after the attack the detachment stayed there and continued work with the reconnaissance and with the preparations, and when the people who were in charge of the reconnaissance and the preparations went, they saw that the attack could take place that then it actually did take place. And this happened on the 27th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what was the objective of this operation that commenced on 27 May 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective was to liberate three features in that area, 726, 702, and 706.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, who made the determination that those three features were the -- were to be the objective of this 27 May 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order came from the command of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how that order was transmitted to the detachment? How did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the form, whether it came in the form of mail delivered at the gates of the detachment or through electronic media or through Paket communication. I don't remember exactly. I didn't pay much attention to that. In any event, the order arrived for the detachment to move from one area, from Sarici to Zavidovici, and to carry out the preparations and then carry out the liberation of these three features.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, about any preparatory meetings that were held prior to the commencement of the May 27, 1995, operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we leave aside 1994, that is what happened then, there were at least two meetings before the attack was carried out. We have been mentioning the preparations, and the old order was in force, that is to carry out the attack. And the participants who -- were to hold other locations, but this particular attack was to be carried out by our detachment only. We only had the assistance of the local unit that was there on the front line and the assistance of manpower to carry the wounded. They were work platoons and so on. At the last meeting it was decided when the attack would be launched. The particular date and hour was fixed for the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you some follow-up questions about these two meetings. Do you recall, sir, approximately when the first meeting was and where that meeting was?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Perhaps in the corps command. But the second one was certainly in Zavidovici. Whether it was at the forward command post or the division command I'm not quite sure, but in any case, it was in the area. The first one was perhaps in the corps command, but I'm not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall, again focusing your attention on the first meeting, do you recall who attended that meeting? Who was in attendance?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the part of the detachment there was Abu Mali, the commander; Muatez; I as the interpreter. On behalf the corps command there was Sakib Mahmuljin. If the meeting was held at the corps headquarters, then only Sakib Mahmuljin was present, but I'm not 100 per cent sure where the meeting was held. If it was in Zavidovici, then Hasanagic would have been present as commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you about the second meeting. Can you tell us approximately when -- how -- how much time before the combat began that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been about two days before the attack, because it was stated that the unit was ready for the attack, the date was fixed. Not the hour, because -- we didn't fix the hour because everything depended on the situation on the ground, whether it would be possible to do it at 4.00 or 5.00 or 6.00. Everything depended on the local situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us who attended this second meeting in the end of May 1995, before the operations began on the 27th of May?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the corps commander was present and the division commander. The commander of the 3rd Corps, Sakib Mahmuljin, and the commander of the 35th Division, Fadil Hasanagic. Abu Mali was present as the commander of the El Mujahedin, and Muatez, responsible for military affairs, and I was present as the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, once those operations commenced on 27 May 1995, where were you located at that time?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the forward command post of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and this post, I think it was called Gluha Bukva. I'm not quite sure. Anyway, it was below or at the foot of feature 726. Above the village called Livade and below the 726 feature. I was at the forward command post there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, who else from the detachment was at that forward command post?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, Abu mail, myself and somebody in charge of communications who was a member of the detachment. I think the place was called Suplja Bukva. I think that's better. Not Gluha Bukva but Suplja Bukva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You just mentioned that at this forward command post there was someone who was responsible for communications. Can you tell us a little bit about the communication systems that the detachment had? Again, in May 1995.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had our communications centre linking together all the assault groups, the groups that were to attack, and each of the leaders of those groups had a Motorola, the emir of the group, and he was connected to the communications centre. Then we also had a link with another Motorola that was not linked to this one, connected to the division command or to the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, if you know whether those communication systems during May 1995, during those operation -- or the operation in May 1995, were these communication systems functioning?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to a point, yes. It was difficult to establish communication because the Chetniks were interfering in our frequencies, and we weren't always able to communicate well with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What about communication with the 35th Division or the 3rd Corps during this operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as you start speaking on the Motorola they would sometimes put a music in, sometimes insults. As soon as they discovered the frequency, they would start interfering.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what role or what you were doing personally when this May 1995 operation was underway?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present next to the commander. If one of the participants in the attack were to send a message or if something had to be passed on in Bosnian, I would do that, or if someone was speaking in Bosnian, I would interpret to the commander and pass on the orders. If it was necessary to establish connection with division command or their communication centre to ask for artillery support, then I would do so using the Motorola that was linked to the division command. We rarely spoke to the corps command. This was just in case of necessity. If I failed to establish contact with the division centre, then I would try and contact the corps command, but that was very rarely done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned artillery support from the division. Do you recall whether any such requests were made for artillery support during the May 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we only had very modest artillery, that is one 120-millimetre mortar and two 80-millimetres mortars, then we asked for artillery support, ZIS guns or the support of a tank or a howitzer which we didn't have. And since the division did have such an artillery unit, we would ask for their support.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: A few moments ago, sir, you made mention of a local unit being involved in this operation or being along the lines during this operation. Can you tell us a little bit more about what unit that was?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the question. I don't quite understand the Serbian language, so could we have Bosnian language if possible? She's using a word that I don't understand in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand Serbian too well. Could I please have Bosnian language or Arabic? That would be fine. I really don't understand too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me -- let me try to ask the question again. A few moments ago when you told us about this May 1995 operation, you mentioned a local unit assisting the El Mujahedin Detachment, and I'm wondering if you can recall when you say a local unit, do you know what unit that was and can you tell us a little bit more about what that unit was doing during the May 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local unit was the 328th Brigade that held the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We're trying to attend to the problem that Mr. Awad has raised. It does seem as if we do not have at this moment a Bosnian-speaking interpreter in the booth. We can only -- we only have that one who speaks Serbian, and I don't -- there is actually nothing we do at this stage to resolve the problem. Have you been able to -- to resolve that word that you didn't understand that was mentioned in Serbian, Mr. Awad, with the interpreter, or at least with Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood when you talk about a local unit, because you need to understand the following -- oh, all right. You need to understand when you say the word "mesna jedinica [phoen]," it means "meso," "meat," from what I understand, but it can be "mejesna jedinica," meaning "local unit." But when you say "mesna" without the J, I think it's made some -- that it's something made of meat. Then I lose my concentration and I cannot speak. I need to understand perfectly what is coming to me through the earphones, and then I can answer the questions properly, and that's how I can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand. My question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that the question had to do with the local unit that was there, and I started to answer that question, that this unit was the 328th Brigade, that this was its area of responsibility. They were holdings that line, that place where the attack was launched from on the 27th of May, 1995. They didn't have a major role. They were just there as a rear support, because when you capture, God willing, the area that is being attacked, then somebody needs to come close to form a new line. And then they can participate in guards these positions, in holding these new positions, because when an attack is carried out and the terrain a captured -- may I proceed? When an attack is carried out and terrain is captured, the forces themselves, or the El Mujahedin Detachment, because they're not a large force, somebody is needed to cover and guard and hold that terrain, digging trenches, fortifications, and so on. So this is the sort of support I was talking about in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Awad, about what happened when this attack was launched?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: When members of the El Mujahedin Detachment managed to reach enemy positions, I think that at one point a part of the unit that was close was discovered and the action began some 15 minutes earlier than it was supposed to. In a very short period thanks to Allah Jelashan [phoen], they managed to capture three elevations, to drive away the enemy forces, and to capture new positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, about any reporting that might have happened after these three features were taken?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean in the sense of reporting? By whom? Can we specify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, once these three features were taken, did the detachment report what had happened to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the evening a meeting was held at the division command -- or perhaps the meeting was held in the Panorama restaurant, actually, and that's when it was reported that the operation was successful. Then we reported about how many casualties we had, how many killed and wounded, and what else was needed in order to maintain the success, what was necessary, which forces should come and -- so that they can later relieve the detachment forces that carried out the assault and the preparations, and then at the meeting it was said what else needed to be done in order to maintain. For example, do we need some tools, digging tools, saws in order to fortify the lines. And then later, perhaps, the local unit that was holding the area could take over from the Mujahedin in that area. Of course the detachment would not withdraw fully. Some people would stay in order to preserve the line, but a large number could be withdrawn so that they could rest and prepare new operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when this meeting took place, sir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same evening, I said. The attack was on the 27th of May in the morning, and the meeting was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander, Sakib Mahmuljin. The commander of the 3rd Corps was there, Fadil Hasanagic. The commander of the 35th Division, Abu Mali; the commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment, Muatez, who was responsible for military questions. I was there as the interpreter. I don't know else who was there. Maybe some others. Maybe the commander of the 328th Brigade. Maybe he was there. I don't remember the other people who -- who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Awad, when this May 1995 operation had a name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, Mr. Awad says he is not Ajwad, he's Awad, Awad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall whether this operation in May 1995 had a name or a title?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation when it was carried out didn't have any names, but after it was carried out successfully, the operation, the press centre -- or, rather, the press service in the El Mujahedin Detachment named it as the operation Elfat El Mubeen [phoen], meaning "Clear Victory."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This press service or press department of the El Mujahedin Detachment, can you tell us a little bit about -- a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This service worked on the promotion of the El Mujahedin Detachment's work, meaning that they even tried to publish a paper or a bulletin that the members of the detachment could read. They could read about their successes and so on. So the press service worked on the promotion of the work of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention now, sir, to the second operation. Do you recall the date that the second major operation in 1995 commenced?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of July, 1995, was when the operation began.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the objective of the operation that began on 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective of the operation was to capture the three elevations, the three elevations 551. Elevation 551, these are three elevations that are facing the Paljenik hill, close to Paljenik hill. But there are several details about this action, and if you wish, I can tell the details. And if you wish, you can also ask me specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll just to that in just a moment. Can you tell us, sir, how the detachment determined the objective for this July 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly what I wanted to tell you about these details. The El Mujahedin Detachment, after the Elfat El Mubeen operation, started with reconnaissance farther along of the surrounding terrain towards the Cevljusa peak or ridge. I think that's what it was called. The detachment was getting ready for an attack in that direction. However - I don't know why - there was a change in the plan, and we were informed by the command, the corps command and the division command, that the priority was to attack along a different axis, meaning those three elevations, in to create pre-conditions for a further attack towards Paljenik, the facility overseeing the main road linking Zavidovici, Zenica, Tuzla. Of course the detachment then turned its reconnaissance towards that facility rather than the previously prepared reconnaissance for the previous target. The attack was carried out on the 21st of July, and it was successful, and those three features were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us whether in that period between the operation on 27 May 1995, and the operation on 21 July 1995, any meetings were held with the detachment and either the division or the corps?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite normal, because we received -- we were told to change our direction of reconnaissance from the one that we were carrying out before towards Kvrge and the other place. We were told to go to different features. This is 551, elevation 551. So before that there was definitely a meeting with the corps commander, and later for sure there was one with the division command who was assisting. They were simply providing support to us because we needed scouts, people who knew the terrain, who would show us the axis of reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, when this meeting with the 3rd Corps commander took place prior to the July 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but it was definitely in late June when the meeting was held. That was when we were given the recommendation to change our direction. So it was probably in the second half of that month, not in the first half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than the El Mujahedin detachment, sir, were there other units of the ARBiH involved in this operation on 21 July?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the attack, no other unit took place. Perhaps they provided support in terms of later when the terrain was captured, but no one took part in the actual attack other than members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me then ask you, sir, about this meeting with the 35th Division commander before the July operation. Do you recall approximately when that meeting took place and where?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably there were several meetings, not just one. Perhaps the most important was the one before the action itself when this meeting was held asking or deciding that the unit was ready for the attack and that the attack could be carried out on that day, and then it was said what was necessary to be done. Sometimes we needed to secure the area. For example, if there was no good road to bring in food, we would ask for the road to be built. We would use equipment to make it possible to pull out safely, to pull out the wounded. We always took care of that. We never allowed any of our wounded to suffer on the road. We would always find a situation or a solution so that people could reach the nearest medical service as quickly as possible so that they could be sent on to the hospital later. And the meetings were probably held also before this last meeting to secure all of these conditions. And then there was probably a meeting for last preparations to determine the time of attack and other details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, where these meetings were held?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly there were some at the division command. And the last meeting was definitely either at the IKM or at the division commandment possibly it was at the IKM of the 35th Division. I don't remember where it was exactly. Maybe after Zavidovici at the Panorama or some other place. I don't remember precisely, but I know that the meetings were held.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who attended these meetings?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a standard thing. The El Mujahedin Detachment commander Abu Mali, Muatez, myself as the interpreter, the commander of the 35th Division. I'm not sure here whether the corps commander was here. I'm not sure. I really doesn't say for sure if the corps commander was there. Maybe he wasn't even there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once this operation commenced on 21 July 1995, where were you on that day, Mr. Awad?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was supposed to take part in the attack, because I was the interpreter the whole time, but then I insisted. I also wanted to experience a bit of the fighting. I was there to fight, too, not just to be an interpreter, but I was used because I knew that Bosnian language and so on. Since I stayed late with the preparations of the people who were preparing the operation, I stayed with the doctor late, until 2.00 in the morning, who was arranging the pull-out of the wounded, how to carry them away, so I was there. And when I finished all of that, the group that I was supposed to go with in the field had already reached their attack positions and it was not possible for them to catch up with them. In the morning when the attack was carried out, I was below the line of attack, below the line where the 325th Brigade was holding its positions. And when I reached that place, when we got there, the attack had just started and there was no more the opportunity to do anything, to join. So at the time of the attack, I was at the line itself from where the attack was launched, or I was just in front of the place from where the attack was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how the attack unfolded on the 21st of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was there on the line I came with Adnan Pezo most probably, who was leading the operation, and when the attack began he received an immediate report saying that the line was broken through and that it was okay to come. Since he was familiar with the terrain, he immediately set off to the place and I followed him, but there was a steep incline. And he was a light person, a fit person. I'm a bit more corpulent and I couldn't run, so I got a bit tired. And we reached the first dugout that had been captured, that had been cleared, and I stayed there. He continued forward, and I stayed at that place. Since I was tired, I entered the dugout to rest a little, and I fell asleep there, and I only woke up once the operation was all over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us -- can you tell us, how would you characterise that operation on 21 July 1995 in terms of the objectives of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation was very successful. When I heard from these people, the members of our group who was there near the dugout, that a large area of the terrain was captured, that a tank was captured, it was a major success. The first time that we had captured a tank. It was a large, major success. And in the course of the operation, Allah made it so that those who were holding -- the Chetniks who were holding the positions, when they heard our Tekbir that we had broken through the line at that place, they fled from the terrain that we were reconnoitering earlier. So the elevation 551, that entire area was empty. They had left that area, and nobody remained in that area, so that we immediately captured their positions and a major success was achieved. The area was 13 kilometres wide that was captured, while the actual attack was carried out in a very narrow area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned capturing the front lines and capturing this Serb tank. Do you know during the July 1995 operation if any prisoners of war were taken?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were any captured, I saw two people who were captured being led by an Arab who was about a metre and a half. And there was another person who was very tall. He was a doctor. He was almost two metres tall. When I saw them, I told that Arab guy that those two captured men should be taken to the first place of assembly. I think that was in the village of Livade, the place of assembly for the unit. And I asked him to take them to the place. After that, I no longer saw the people who were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, approximately where you were when you saw this Arab escorting these two prisoners?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say "Arabs." I saw one Arab.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's what I think I said. When you saw this Arab, singular, Arab, escorting the two prisoners of war, do you recall approximately where you were when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the precise point when I came to the first dugout where I stayed there to wait, before I entered the dugout to rest I saw those two persons, and then I told him that. After that I entered the dugout and sat down, and then after, I fell asleep there. I don't know exactly what the name of it. I don't know the terrain, so I don't know exactly what that place was called, but it was the first dugout some hundred -- some 500 metres out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Awad, do you recall approximately what time it was on the 21st of July, 1995, when you saw these two prisoners being escorted?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 6.00 in the morning. Immediately in the morning. As soon as the action started. But there is one detail before the action. We -- this has to be said so that people could listen and hear what happened. I remember that someone set the time the attack would be carried out so that the Chetniks were bombarding the positions all night, and the line that was held where our fighters managed to get to, but none of our fighters were wounded in this shelling. Later, I found out that Ivo Lozancic, who was the commander of the HVO in Zepce, he was -- since there was a Joint Command of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the HVO, I heard that he actually issued those -- that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, other than these two prisoners of war that you personally observed, did you ever come to learn about any other prisoners taken during the July 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not encounter any prisoners. However, after the operation - I don't know how much time had passed - I though that an exchange was carried out, and I think that 11 prisoners were handed over to the military police of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know any of the details about this hand-over of these 11 prisoners to the 3rd Corps military police?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't take part in the exchange. I kind the report saying that the prisoners had been taken over, and my signature is there, and I think I handed it over to the military police, but I didn't directly take part in that exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, sir, about any meeting or meetings that immediately followed the operations on 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you? Just before you move on to point, Mr. Mundis, you asked the witness if he had got to learn about any other POWs after those two. The answer that was given in the English channel set, "I did not encounter any POWs." I'm not quite sure whether, apart from encountering them, the witness has ever heard or come to learn, as you had asked, of any other POWs. I would like to know whether he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you understand what -- what the Presiding Judge has asked?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood your question, both questions, if I understood them correctly, you're asking did I see any other prisoners. I did not. I only saw those two prisoners. I did not see any other prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you hear about any other prisoners being taken on 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: These ones that were handed over, the prisoners who were handed over to the military police of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, those people were the ones who were captured in that action, but I personally did not see others except those two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We understand, Mr. Awad, that you did not see any POWs. The question is, did you come to hear of any other POWs that were captured on the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that other people were captured, the ones who were exchanged. I heard that some were captured, and they were exchanged later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you come to hear how many were captured on the 21st of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't how many were captured. I heard of the prisoners who were exchanged. I don't know how many were captured. Perhaps it was just those who had been captured. I don't believe that there were more. Then you would hear that there were more prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Awad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, do you recall whether there were any meetings held immediately after the operation on 21 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would usually and meeting after the operation. Now, whether was that was the same day or the next day, I can't say. There was a meeting, and then the report would be submitted about the success of the operation and everything else that happened during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you personally present at any such meeting following the July 1995 operation?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall where this meeting was and who attended?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 35th Division, our commander Abu Mali, Muatez, and myself. I don't know who else was present, but I can't be more specific as to who else was present. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, the 21 July 1995 operation, did that have a name?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was given a name after it was completed. It was called Al Karame [phoen], which in Bosnian would mean some supernatural thing that happened. That would be the way one could interpret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what language is Al Karame.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Arabic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that name Al Karame was started, an EMD name of the operation? Was the name of the operation given by the El Mujahedin Detachment and not by the -- by the army itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The army didn't give it any name. They may have had another name, but I don't know. But the army didn't give it any name for this operation. It was after the success of the operation, when the attack was completed successfully, in view of the fact that a large area had been captured, maybe -- we had taken over seven kilometres of the front line without any combat because the Chetniks had fled. We called it Al Karame, because it was a supernatural event. In Arabic that is what it means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I do hear. And when you say "we called it," you mean the El Mujahedin Detachment. Thank you. That's all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now, with the assistance of the usher, that the witness be shown Exhibit 1049, which I believe in the binder is still labelled as PT02329. PT02329, which has subsequently been admitted into evidence as Exhibit 1049.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you have this document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention, sir, to paragraph 2, which starts with the letters N/S. Do you see that part of the document?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, about what's being reported in this paragraph? I do have an additional hard copy of this document if that would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here that defence positions are being consolidated and reinforced, and MTS replenishment is being -- being carried out. After the arrival of the El Mujahedin Detachment, further infantry attacks were successfully repulsed. According to incomplete figures, the casualties suffered in the combat activities so far were as follows: Killed 2, missing 5, and wounded 11. That is what this document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you -- do you know, sir, or can you comment upon the reference to the detachment and infantry attacks being successfully repelled?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably the reference here is to the event when the detachment left the front line and handed it over to the local unit, 328th Brigade. A day later - this didn't last long - the Chetniks carried out an attack and made a breakthrough the line that we had already captured. We were informed of this. And then we attacked again trying to stop that attack, and after that there was no further progress made by the Chetniks. And we also came across the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, when you say, "We were informed about this," can you tell us who informed you about these developments?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, whether it was the division command or the corps command I can't remember. The news arrived, anyway, probably from the division command that we should react to this attack to prevent any further progress by the Chetniks. I am more prone to believe that it came from the division command rather than the 3rd Corps command of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, how much longer is the direct examination still to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm attempting to move as quickly as possible, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- dropping topics. I would think probably one more hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've taken four hours already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir -- Witness, can you tell us about the third operation in 1995? When did that operation occur?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation was on the 10th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did this operation have a name?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. This operation was called Farz. That was the designation it was given in the maps, Farz.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know, sir --

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: F-a-r-z.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, who gave that operation the name Farz?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know with precision who gave the operation the name. I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, what was the objective of the El Mujahedin Detachment in operation Farz on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The objective of the El Mujahedin Detachment was to gain control of the Paljenik feature. Popovo Osoje or something like that, and Malovan. The main attack was of the Paljenik hill. It is a bare hill, a clearing. There are no trees on it. And the detachment attacked this feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, who determined that the objective of this attack on 10 September 1995 was to be the Paljenik feature?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a broader operation. Several units took part and several corps. Participating in this operation were two corps, the 3rd Corps and the 2nd Corps in coordination, each attacking from its own side. There were several units of the 3rd Corps. They participated in this operation in -- the El Mujahedin, the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion, and I think the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion, the 329th Brigade, the 7th Muslim Brigade. This was a very large area and a large-scale operation that was carried out on the 10th of September, 1995. And the objectives were set by the command of the 3rd Corps, and the objectives were issued to all units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how those objectives were communicated to these various units that you've described?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the other units, but we received the order after consultations about this large-scale operation and that reconnaissance should be carried out. And when we agreed to participate in the operation, we received the order to carry out the attack in that direction, and we were told that other units would take part of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you ever present, sir, at any meetings where this operation was being planned?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When and where?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first meeting was at the headquarters of the 3rd Corps. The detachment commander Muatez was there, and I was present. Sakib Mahmuljin was there, the commander of the 3rd Corps. At this meeting we discussed the possibilities, but we had already started preparations and were doing reconnaissance in the area. In view of the fact that we were there in place, then we were given this part of the area, Paljenik. We ourselves wished to participate because we had some -- we felt that with guards assistance we could achieve it if the reconnaissance was done properly. This was the first meeting, and after these consultations we felt it would be a good thing for us to do it, and we accepted, and after that the order came. Then came other meetings. Now, whether it was at the headquarters of the 35th Division or at the forward command post, I think there was even a meeting with the commander of the 35th Division at his forward command post. I think it was 777, feature 777. It was called Klek. And we were there at the forward command post, and we discussed these preparations. So there were several meetings before the actual attack was launched in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, approximately what time the attack was launched on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning. We usually attack at dawn. Early in the morning we started the attack. I can't tell you exactly what time it was. 4.00 or 4.15, 4.25. Anyway, early in the morning, before dawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And where were you located? Where were you physically present at the time this attack commenced in the early morning of 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the forward command post of the El Mujahedin Detachment command, which was across the way from the Paljenik hill. I was in this dugout, which was the forward command post. I was with the commander, Abdul El Mali [as interpreted], and Sheik Abwa [phoen] was also present, and there was from the command of the 35th Division, but I can't remember his name. But anyway, I was there at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. Let me -- let me ask you, sir, the interpreter didn't catch all the names of the people who were present in this dugout. Can you repeat the names?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen carefully, please. I was there as the interpreter. The commander Abu El Mali; Sheik Anwar Shaaban; and a signalsman, I think his name was Moris [phoen], who was working with the equipment; and someone on behalf of the 35th Division. I only saw him once in my life, and I didn't remember his name. As some sort of support or coordinator. I don't know. He was there with us. Now, why he was there, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, about the operation on 10 September 1995? What happened?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the Allah's permission the members of the El Mujahedin Detachment attacked and in only four minutes they managed to get controlled of the Paljenik feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And after taking or seizing the Paljenik feature, what did the detachment do?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not just Paljenik. Then there were places to the right, Malovar [phoen], Pod Malovar, Popovo Osoje. This whole area could not be seized at the same time. There were -- there was a fog, so it was not possible to reach all the trenches. So there was some delay, but the main feature was seized in only four minutes. The others were supposed to attack from other directions, and a part of the El Mujahedin Detachment, I think together with the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion who were attached to us just then, managed to reach the asphalt road and to move forward to seize the rest of the area from enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: While this attack was underway on 10 September 1995, what were you personally doing?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said that I was the interpreter, I was interpreting for the commander if he doesn't understand something, or passing on his comments. I was some sort of a coordinator when people on the ground were asking for support. For instance, if artillery support was required, I would react directly and ask the communications centre of the 35th Division for this artillery support. Since the objectives were set in advance and given numbers, I would ask for support at number 35, 42, 17. I would ask for such support. If there was some sort of delay or any problem, I would, in a sense, coordinate these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Awad, whether there were any meetings after this operation took place on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is normal for a meeting to be held, to report on the operation, whether it was successful or not, what kind of problems were encountered. There was quite normal to have a meeting of that kind. And all the participants would be present, the corps commander, the division commander, the commanders of the units, for each one of them to report what they had done, what difficulties they had encountered, what degree of success had been achieved, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you say it would be -- it would be normal, but my question is was there such a meeting on 10 September 1995, after the operations were complete?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding the 10th of September, there may have been one in the evening. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember attending any such meeting on 10 September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly whether it was on the 10th, but there was a meeting, and I did attend. Now, whether it was the same evening after the operation or the next day, I'm not sure. So I want to be very precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, sir, where was this meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was held at the forward command post of the 35th Division, which was in the Babylon restaurant on the road Krivaja, the villages called Krivaja, and I think this building is in Krivaja, and that is where that meeting was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, sir, who attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, Sakib Mahmuljin; the commander of the 35th Division, Fadil Hasanagic; the commander of El Mujahedin, Abu El Mali; I was present; a commander of the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion, of the 4th Manoeuvre Battalion of the 328th Brigade; 329th Brigade. Anyway, all the commanders of all the units that took part in this operation attended this meeting. That is my recollection of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, in this time period, the first two weeks of September 1995, were you ever in the town of Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I didn't hear it quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you, sir, ever personally present in the town of Vozuca during the first two weeks of September 1995?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first two weeks. I was after the 10th of September in Vozuca, yes. That is the day I entered Vozuca, when it was liberated, but not before. It wasn't the 1st, 2nd or 3rd of September but on the 10th of September. When Vozuca was liberated, I entered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And why did you enter Vozuca after that town was liberated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But that's not all he said. He said he entered Vozuca on the 10th when it was to be liberated, not after it was liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I -- I heard him to say after it was liberated, but I can ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, who controlled Vozuca when you entered the town, when you went there?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was the reason, sir, that you went to Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accompanied the commander afternoon when the territory had been liberated. It was free territory. Everybody wanted to see what had been liberated and what had been done. So I was escorting the commander. And I saw this place that was liberated, prompted by the desire to see what had been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you and the commander have any meetings or briefings in Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, no, and in that location, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you return to Vozuca at any point in time after this first day that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the late President Alija Izetbegovic visited Vozuca. I, with the commander, was present during that visit, and that is when I visited Vozuca again. It may not have been Vozuca it, or a location close to it. I considered all that area as Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us a little bit about this visit of the late President Izetbegovic to Vozuca when you were present?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late President Alija Izetbegovic when he visited, he came to thank the fighters of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina for their great success, because they had managed to liberate a large territory and to link two towns which were cut off for a long time, that is the towns of Zenica and Tuzla, and to link two corps, the 3rd and 2nd Corps. They liberated a large area of territory, and he addressed -- addressed the soldiers with words of praise, and he congratulated them on this success.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, who was present on this day in Vozuca other than yourself and the commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the late President Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the late president had spoken, there was a group of people next to a map when the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, the commander of the 2nd Corps of the BH army, the commander of the 35th Division of the BH army, also present was the commander of the El Mujahid Detachment, and some other people were present. A lot of people were present there. And when the commanders explained to the president and indicated the area that had been liberated, the new positions that had taken up by the army, and they informed the president that the operations were continuing in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. This would be an appropriate spot for the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it a convenient time for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, earlier we were talking about the prisoners of war from the July 1995 operation, and I'd like to ask you if you were ever aware of any prisoners of war taken during the September 1995 operation.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask at this point in time that the witness be shown the document that's been marked P02582, P02582. And I would ask if the usher could please though the Arabic version of this document to the witness. Yeah. I have -- I have hard copies here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what this document is?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says something here in Arabic, like some kind of declaration or some sort of report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, who produced this document?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell from the information contained at the top of the document?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you what is written, but I don't know what is the source of the document. I can just read what it says at the top of the paper, but I don't know if that's the source of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise, sir -- do you see any stamps or other markings on the document that are familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upper right-hand corner there is some kind of sign. There are two rifles which are leaning, one on top of the other, and there's something in the middle that's quite indistinct. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the original could be placed on the ELMO. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know what that marking on the upper right-hand corner of this document is?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see two rifles there, and there's something in the middle, but I cannot really say exactly what that is. There are two rifles. It's not clear, the image. You can see the two rifles, and there's something in the middle. What that is in the middle is something that I'm not familiar with. I don't really see it all that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what the subject of this document is or what's written there in the large Arabic script in the middle of the document?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Arabic it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said something in Arabic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the Operation Badr Bosna [phoen], or "The capture of Vozuca," and then below that there is another declaration or something. It says "Second declaration."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not see the -- the English translation on the screen, we note.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, have you ever heard of the battle of Badr before, or can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Badr Bosna -- Bosnia is something I did hear of. It's a name of the third operation that was carried out on the 10th of September, 1995. As far as the Mujahedin were concerned, after the conquest the operation was called Badr Bosna. The operation was actually called Farz, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who gave -- who gave this operation this name Badr?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The detachment press service would give the operations a name. It would name the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, to whom the press service or department of the El Mujahedin Detachment was forwarding information to?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not all that familiar with it. They would issue a daily bulletin for the detachment, and they would send information to the Islamic world.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Why would they do that, send information to the Islamic world?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, the whole world was following the events in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The El Mujahedin Detachment received donations for -- donations from the Islamic world, from the Muslims in the Islamic world, and for those Muslims to be happy with some successes that happened in Bosnia and Herzegovina, to alleviate the sadness, the press service would send reports to the Islamic world in order to inform them a little bit about the situation in Bosnia, especially if there was some happy news like success and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, do you see at the bottom of this document under -- in Bosnian under the phrase "Odred El Mujahedin" do you see some writing?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "12 April, BB Street."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you -- do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that it document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honours. I believe that with this witness not sufficient ground was established in order to admit this exhibit as an exhibit. The witness actually said that he sees a document written in Arabic. He read the heading of the document in Arabic, which anyone could have done who speaks the Arab language -- Arabic language. No other element of this document was confirmed by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness was able to identify the subject of this document and indicated that that was a term or name that was used to describe the operation, and other than that the document, we would suggest, speaks for itself in terms of the contents of the document and -- and what was -- what is contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that not sufficient basis has been laid for the admission of the document. The document will not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask Your Honours that it be given a marked for identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the document be marked for identification and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark this document for identification as Exhibit 1129.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: MFI 1129. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown P02669, P02669. And again I would ask perhaps if the Arabic could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to focus your -- I'd like to focus your attention on the stamps that are appearing on this document. Do you recognise those markings?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll move on then, Your Honours. This document can be withdrawn from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to a different subject with you, Mr. Awad, and that concerns the issue of training, military training. Can you tell us a little bit about any military training that was conducted during the time period you were a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you too many details since I did not go through such training, but generally speaking the training carried out in the El Mujahedin Detachment was training on light weaponry, maybe the use of RPGs, mortars, and so on, and also some tactical training in the sense of how combat actions are executed and so on. This is what I can generally say about that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, about any military training at Hotel Ruda in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which hotel?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Ruda.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no Ruda hotel in Zenica. There is no Hotel Ruda in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, of any training for military officers of the ARBiH conducted in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're thinking of the military officers' school called Ros, it was organised for the military officers in Zenica, and it was organised in the Hotel Rudar in Zenica. There is no Ruda hotel in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is in fact the training I was referring to. My mistake as to the name of the hotel. Can you tell us a little bit about that training course?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything. I didn't attend that military officers' school. I wasn't present there, so I can't say much about it. Of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether anyone from the El Mujahedin Detachment received training at that school in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know we sent two men who were members of the El Mujahedin detachment for the training, Ismet Fazlic and Norudin [phoen] Alihodze, and they completed that war school for military officers, the name of which was Ros.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, do you know why or can you tell us why these two individuals, Ismet Fazlic and Norudin Alihodze were sent to this school?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to become officers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown the document P01887, P01887.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document refers to?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names are given here, Alihodze Nahazim [phoen] Norudin, and Fazlic Hamdija Ismet, that they are being admitted to Ros.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the document on the screen please be shifted so that we can see what -- no, no, the English. You may proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us again what this document refers to?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to read the contents. I just read the names out, but I haven't read the contents. It's an order here saying that two cadets, members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, are being sent to the Ros.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just, sir, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, do you know what Ros stands for?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said earlier. It's the war military officers' school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it be please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 1130, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Awad, you told us yesterday that you were a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment until that unit was demobilised. Sir, do you recall when you first were informed or became aware that the El Mujahedin Detachment was to be demobilised?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I heard of it was at the meeting with the late President Alija Izetbegovic. The meeting took place in Zenica, in the old -- the pensioners' hall. He said that the Dayton agreement would be signed and that the detachment wouldn't exist any more, that it would need to be dismantled, and that the people needed to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the approximate date or time period of this meeting at Dom Penzionera in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in December 1995. In any case, it was before the signing of the Dayton Accords, before the 14th of December. I'm not sure exactly which day it was, but I know it took place before, this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, other than the late President Izetbegovic who attended this meeting in December 1995 at Dom Penzionera?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was attended by General Rasim Delic, General Sakib Mahmuljin. Detachment commander Abu El Mali was there, and Sheik Enver Ahmed Sunali [phoen], and I was there as the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, any of the specific topics of conversation at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: They talked to the late president about -- well, when he told us that the Dayton Accords would be signed, that the fighting would stop, there would be no more fighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that the detachment had to be dismantled, and that according to the Dayton agreement all foreigners must leave Bosnia and Herzegovina, in any case, this topic was discussed, and Abu Mali and Sheik Enver spoke with the president, Izetbegovic, that there was no need. It was possible to fight. The army had advanced. It had a lot of successes and that perhaps this peace would not be good for these people. However, the late president stood by his position that the accords had to be signed and that the war had to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, if General Delic spoke at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any direct contacts with him. When they talked with the late president, because they wanted to see if he would yield a little bit in his position, then General Delic would say, "President, do you remember what we agreed in December?" That was the only sentence of his during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, on any other occasion before the signing of the Dayton agreement if there was a second such meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With the same general group of individuals that you've just told us about.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that there was a meeting with General Delic, but there was a meeting with the President Alija Izetbegovic, the late president. It was a meeting in the Zavidovici Division building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was the subject of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The late president toured the terrain. He was touring the municipality of Zavidovici, and he stopped by the division command building where the commanders of the units that were in that area were there. We were also there, and we had a meeting with the president alone. We spoke with him for 15 minutes. This meeting was attended by Abu Mali and myself as the interpreter representing the Mujahedin detachment; the commander of the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sakib Mahmuljin, was present; and the late President Alija was present. In the meantime, Sheik Ehmed [as interpreted] Shaaban also joined the meeting, who came from Zenica. He was not in Zavidovici, but he came from Zenica later. We were informed about the president's meeting quite late, so he couldn't come by car, so he managed to get from Zenica to Zavidovici by helicopter. I am speaking about the late Sheik Enver.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document P03058, P03058. And I'm interested in page 2 of the Bosnian document, and the bottom of page 2 and top of page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to read the first two paragraphs of this document, and then I'd ask you to comment upon what's contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment, sir, upon the information reported in these two paragraphs of this document?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that on the 10th of December, 1995, two working meetings were held with representatives of the El Mujahedin Unit. The first was held at the 3rd Corps command with the commander of the General Staff of the BH army, and the commander of 3rd Corps being present. And the second meeting was also attended, apart from these two, by the president of the republic. On behalf of El Mujahedin was Abu Mali and his assistant for security, Awad Ajman, and Sheik Enver Shaaban. I mentioned a moment ago the meeting in the pensioners' home. I remember that one. I really don't remember this meeting in the corps command. I remembered the meeting in the pensioners' home. It was after half past 7.00. The main news programme is at half past 7.00. So we were sitting with the president in the pensioners' home, and as is stated here, it was noted that the unit had to be disbanded. I really do not recall this first meeting. I simply don't remember that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But the information in the second paragraph, does that accurately reflect what you remember happening at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
