utterances.text: It's a poor copy, so I can't see all the words. I have already said that we were told that it had to be disbanded as soon as possible and pursuant to the talks in Dayton. I said that a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the first line of this document refers to the date 10 December 1995.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does that, sir, correspond to the rough time period when you believe this meeting that you've talked about at Dom Penzionera occurred?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite possible. It may have been that particular day. They have better information than I do. The admission of the Presidency took care of case, so it's quite possible that that is the correct date. I just said that it was a meeting held prior to the signing of the Dayton Accords. So I assume that that is the correct date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 1131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Awad, can you perhaps tell us about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How much longer are you going to be? You have finished your hour that you asked for at the end -- before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe we're on about the next to the last topic. I would hope to be finished in about 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, can you explain to us a little bit about what happened from a logistical point of view as the unit was demobilised?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the detachment itself is concerned, in view of the fact that it was being demobilised and there was no need for any weapons and everything else that we held in our possession, we handed this in to the command of the 3rd Corps, to the command of the 3rd Corps as we no longer needed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And why -- why were those weapons handed over to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, these weapons had to be left to someone. You can't leave it in the hands of people in the streets to avoid killings. So we had to return it to an organisation, somebody who would take care of that weaponry, and it was best for it to be handed in to the 3rd Corps command, which would take care of that weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown P02873, P02873. And I'm primarily interested in page 2 of the Bosnian and page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, if you could please look at that part of the document that is numbered 5, which deals with logistics support. Do you see the bullet point referring to the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just started reading it. Just a moment, please. I see that it says El Mujahedin here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment upon what's written on this document, sir, in terms of what you've just told us about weapons?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the taking over of weapons and explosive ordnance from the El Mujahedin Detachment has been completed. So it says that they've already taken over the weapons. As I said a moment ago, we handed our weapons over to the 3rd Corps, and here they say that this takeover has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was the dinner the following day delicious, sir? The document is gone. It talks about the dinner that was arranged for the El Mujahedin Detachment the following day. I just wanted to know if it was okay, the dinner. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want an answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the biggest dinner, the biggest meal that I ever had in my whole life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll admit the document as Exhibit 1132.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, can you just tell us, if you know, what happened to the Vatrostalna building at the time the detachment was demobilised?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We handed over everything. Even the Vatrostalna building was returned to the command of the 3rd Corps. And I don't know what happened next. The army secured it. Now, what happened to it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown P02864, P02864.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, I would ask you to take a look at the paragraph numbered 1 under the word "Order."

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment upon what's contained in this order under paragraph number 1?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago even without this order we returned the facility. We didn't use it any more. There was no need for it. Since the unit had been demobilised and the men had left Bosnia and Herzegovina, we no longer needed this facility. So even without this order, we had to return it to someone, and since we had received that facility as being part of the army, we returned it to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 1133, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I would be interested in knowing what sort of weaponry did we talk about at the end of the war? How heavy -- or, rather, did the El Mujahid Detachment dispose over heavy artillery, or was it just light infantry weapons, or what are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yeah?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the weaponry is concerned, all the weaponry was returned and handed over. As for heavy weapons, if we have tanks in mind, they were handed over earlier on to the tank unit that was within the 3rd Corps of the BH army, so that the tanks had been handed over earlier on to the services of that unit. As for the other weapons, the infantry weapons and every piece of ammunition was handed over to the logistics of the 3rd Corps, including mortars and everything we had captured in all our operations. We had a small cannon. We had mortars, hand-held rocket launchers. All these things were handed over to the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now that the witness be shown P02848, P02848.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And perhaps, Mr. Awad, if you could just take a quick look at the names on this document. I'm going to then ask you if you recognise any of those names?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I see them, and I recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which -- which names on this document do you recognise, sir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2, Mamdouh Kaber [as interpreted] -- Gaber, Ahmed Mahmoud El Wakil, Abdel Hakim Salem Gouda, Amgad Mohamed Youssef, Ayman Mohamed Youssef. Only those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how do you know those people, sir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got to know them well after the war. For instance, Gaber, we worked together. We did some commercial things. Ahmed Wakil too. He's from Egypt. Abdel Hakim Gouda is a doctor who is in Zenica, who was a doctor in the detachment too. Amgad Mohamed Youssef and his brother Ayman Mohamed Youssef, one went to Great Britain and Angar remained in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In 2001, he was designated as an Egyptian group that Bosnia and Herzegovina should be arrested and handed over to Egypt. He tried to get out of Bosna across the border at Orasje. He was arrested and gaoled because he had false documents. He was imprisoned for four months. After that he was released. His citizenship was confirmed, and he was not extradited to Egypt. And that is how I know these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know -- do you know if any of these people -- or let me rephrase the question. What unit were these people in, if you know, the ones that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Awad, a few moments ago the Presiding Judge asked you about the dinner in Zenica that was referred to in one of the earlier documents. I'd like to ask you a few more questions about that event. Do you recall, sir, the date or day that that dinner took place?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in December, but I don't know the exact date. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of that dinner?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dinner was held in honour of members of the detachment who were leaving Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was simply owning that day in honour of the people leaving Bosnia and Herzegovina, to treat them. There was no other purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there also -- or was there an event in Zenica, sir, that could be characterised as a farewell ceremony?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was there -- was there a formal occasion, sir, at which the El Mujahedin Detachment members attended?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. If we're talking about the dinner, yes, this dinner did take place once. I don't know what else you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where was the dinner?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the army hall, Dom Armija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who attended?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and then there were people from the BH army, General Sakib Mahmuljin was there, General Rasim Delic, Fadil Hasanagic. I think Ahmed Adilovic, and some other people were present there. I can't remember who else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened at that meeting -- or this dinner? Can you tell us about this dinner?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a party. People gathered there, and there were words of praise and gratitude addressed to the people who had come from abroad to assist. I think that some other people spoke. Our commander described who was the Mujahedin, why they had come. A general speech about the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you say that there were words of praise, do you recall who offered these words of praise and what was said?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the speakers were the command of the 3rd -- the commander of the 3rd Corps, General Sakib Mahmuljin; then General Rasim Delic; also Abu Mali. I think Abu Melik was there. I'm not sure. I don't remember. There were -- I can't remember exactly what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, if you can recall, what -- when you say "words of praise," can you -- can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this dinner, if it was organised to express gratitude and to treat these people, means that these people who had fought in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who had come to help the people, they were not criminals. They're leaving, treated by us, that is, by the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They're going home, and they would be treated in this way. So they thanked these people who had come and for coming to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say -- when you say, sir, they thanked these people, who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the organisers of this gathering, and I'm referring to the people who were present at this gathering. Whoever came, he would celebrate the meeting. And if it was organised as a token of gratitude, whoever spoke expressed gratitude to these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, anything that Abu Mali said at that event?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he familiarised those present about the Mujahids, why they had come. He also said what I used to tell my brothers, Bosniaks, that the time would come when people would talk about us, that they would say that we were terrorists and criminals and all kinds of other things. I followed the press, and in 1993 they said that we as the Mujahedin would provoke a fratricidal war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Mujahedin had not come to provoke such conflicts. They had come to assist these people. And such a conflict would never occur our brothers, Muslims, in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So Ali Mali [as interpreted] spoke along the same vein as I had done when speaking to my brothers, Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, do you have any recollection of anything that General Delic said at this event?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he spoke and that he thanked a these men for their success, for their participation. I don't remember anything else that he might have said. That is as much as I can remember, recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe -- can you describe for the Chamber the mood at this dinner, the atmosphere?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just telling the Judge that it was the bitterest dinner I had in my life. The atmosphere was so sad. The people present, especially the Mujahedin, they were all crying, because imagine a man who had come with so much joy to assist and to achieve something, and he had hoped to die on Allah's road, to be a shaheed. His wish is not fulfilled. Somebody stops him, and he has to leave. So something happened that interrupts the achievement of your wish, your goal. So you can imagine how they felt. So the atmosphere was very sad. Nobody cared about the words or the dinner or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Awad, I have a couple of questions concerning an issue that you raised yesterday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, relax a moment. Can we give you a moment, please. Maybe we should take a short adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a short adjournment and come back. --- Break taken at 12.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you -- do you feel better now, Mr. Awad? Thank you so much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I just have a few questions, Mr. Awad, about a subject you raised at the beginning of the hearing yesterday. Can you tell it us, sir, when you became a citizen of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And upon what basis did you become a citizen of BiH?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of laws 23 of 1993. The law says that whoever participates in the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina has the right to the citizenship of the country, and I got my right to the citizenship because I was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I provided the organs with what was requested of me. I met the conditions, and on the basis of that I got my citizenship, on the basis of my participation in the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what were -- if you know, what were the dates of your service in the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you count from the time that I joined the group of Arabs, that's from April, but actually it was from the 13th of August, 1993, until the 25th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could put just one question to the witness before Madam Vidovic takes over. My question relates to the issues that we have been speaking about here lastly, the citizenship and the return of all the members of the El Mujahid Detachment to their respective countries outside Bosnia and Herzegovina. My question is, Mr. Awad, do you know why the El Mujahid members had to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina after the war? We know that it was written directly into the Dayton Accord that all foreigners were to leave the country, and I think this was also what you were told by -- or by the -- this was also what the members of the -- what the leadership of the El Mujahid Detachment was told by the late President Izetbegovic, but what was the reason why the foreigners had to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the real reason is. If those who issued the orders in Dayton said that the volunteers, foreigners, of all sides who participated in the war both on behalf of the army and -- the army of Republika Srpska and the HVO had to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina, I think that was the basis. The second -- well, in my view, why people left Bosnia and Herzegovina was because people came to fight in Bosnia and Herzegovina. When there was no more fighting, there was no need for them to stay. Some returned to their homes. Some went farther. Those persons who were not married, they went to marry. Who had companies, they continued their jobs. Though continued on with their lives. Everybody went their own way. The people in Bosnia and Herzegovina who stayed in Bosnia, they were not subject to the Dayton regulations because they were born in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It did not refer to them. The foreigners had to leave. They had come to fight. There was no more fighting, so there was no more reason for them to stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, if the Bosnian government by law afforded citizenship to them, then they could have stayed, but apparently the Dayton agreement ordered otherwise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot interpret the Dayton Accords. From what I know, the law was that foreigners had to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina, and people who did not wish to stay in Bosnia and Herzegovina left, even those -- some of them who had citizenship of the country, they left. They didn't wish to stay in Bosnia and Herzegovina any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we're going to need a few minutes to distribute the documents, and I would appreciate very much if we could go on our break now so that we could do this now so that we do not take up any court time for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well, then. We'll take a break, and we could -- could we come back at 20 past instead of half past 1.00. Court adjourned. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.22 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you and the witness speak the same language, and we don't have transcript. I'm going to ask you to please make sure you don't overlap. Speak slowly, give him a chance to finish, and ask your question. Mr. Awad, you hear that? Please, when Madam Vidovic is asking you a question, wait until she's finished before you start answering. Okay? Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Awad.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm Vasvija Vidovic, and today I'm going to be putting questions to you on behalf of General Rasim Delic. The nature of cross-examination is such that you would simply be able to answer with a yes or a no to the majority of my questions, and I kindly can you to do so whenever that's possible unless I ask for a more detailed explanation or the Trial Chamber asks you to do that. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I think that you will need to keep your headphones on, because the Judges also might put some questions to you. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, Mr. Awad, you said that you came to Bosnia and Herzegovina in late 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You came via the assistance of the Arab humanitarian organisation Mowafaq; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You came to the Zenica area, and it would be correct to say that you were received there by a representative of the civilian authorities, a certain Mr. Makic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We held a meeting with Mr. Makic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, did you say you came in 1992 or in 1982?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I came to the former Yugoslavia in 1982, but I came to Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992, late 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put one more question to you that has to do with Mr. Makic. At the time, he was the president of the Zenica Executive Board, if you know?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was carrying out that function. I'm not sure about his name, but that is that person who was doing that job, the President of the Executive Board or council - that's what it was called - of the municipality of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, that person received you when you came to Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to put some questions to you about the arrival, the manner of arrival to Bosnia and Herzegovina. I would be correct, would I not, if I were to say that you entered Bosnia and Herzegovina without the mediation of any institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony yesterday, you said that after arriving you joined a group of Arabs accommodated at the Bilmiste school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened in April 1993. Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Regarding that group of Arabs at Bilmiste, I would like to ask you this, please: You did not consider that group of Arabs at Bilmiste a part of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a group of Turks that was also accommodated at the Bilmiste school. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not consider them either to be a part of the Muslim 7th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about their status. I cannot say if they were or not part of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thus you have no information that they were a part of the Muslim 7th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday in response to a question by the Prosecutor, you said that you received your first uniform from Mr. Halil Brzina about whom you said that at the time he was the logistics man of the 7th Brigade, and I would like to clarify this with you, please. It's correct, isn't it, that you received the uniform while you were still a humanitarian worker and that you received it as a gift? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that it was like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you did not receive it as a Mujahedin but as a member of a humanitarian organisation. Not as a Mujahedin fighter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I had not yet joined the Mujahedin. I had not yet become one of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to briefly clarify with you the relationship of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the groups that you mentioned, the group of Arabs and Turks that you encountered at Bilmiste. Please, first of all, I'm going to ask you about this group of Arabs that you joined. That group of Arabs did not carry out the orders of the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw was that they were not carrying out the orders of the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall -- actually, I would like to remind you of a statement that you gave to the Prosecutor earlier. First of all, I would like to establish this: Do you recall giving a statement to the Prosecutor in August and September 2005? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Investigator Michael Koehler. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to quote to you paragraph 84 of the statement. Tell me if you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to be citing portions of his statement, and if the witness does not recognise them, I will show them to him then, but otherwise we don't need to waste time on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I am quoting to you the paragraph 84 of your statement. You said -- this is marked as D783. You said: "Arabs were not receiving orders from anyone. They were just going to the front line to fight. Nobody could order the Arabs to go, because they wanted to go to fight anyway, but all of them asked the emir whether to go or not." Do you remember, Mr. Awad, giving a statement to this effect to Mr. Koehler whom you mentioned a little bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the entire statement that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D783.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps -- perhaps while that's being done, to avoid any confusion if my learned colleague could indicate the dates concerning that part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess your learned friend talked about a statement that was made sometime in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm actually not referring to the date of the statement but the time period at which this part of the statement relates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let the witness be shown the statement so that -- and you heard what your learned friend says, Madam Vidovic, if you are able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you please look at paragraph 84.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And in respect of this question by my learned friend Mr. Mundis I would like to ask you this first of all: Which time period were you talking about? First, can you recall giving such a statement to the investigator from the OTP? I'm talking about paragraph 84?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My following question -- my next question is this: Which time period are you talking about in that part of the statement?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about the time before the forming of the El Mujahedin detachment. I was talking about the period from April 1993 that I went through. The investigator insisted on a lot of things, so I talked about that in general, but I don't want to be part of the statement before the date that I actually joined the group of Arabs that was at Bilmiste.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, this part of your statement refers to the period before the founding of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this: What you said in paragraph 84 of your statement was how it actually was, wasn't it? I mean, it's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony you mentioned several times Wahiuddeen, if I am pronouncing the name correctly. Please, Wahiuddeen was the emir of all the Arabs present in Central Bosnia right until his death; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has been wrongly interpreted. He could not have been the emir of all Arabs in the area of Central Bosnia. There was a certain group that was under his command. He was their emir. There were other people who were not under his command and could not be considered -- and could not have considered them as their emir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whatever is may be, I'm talking at this point about this group of Arabs that were under his command. Please, the emir was responsible for the actions and the direction that the Mujahedin had to take even after the formal establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The emir is responsible for his Mujahedin. The emir is responsible for his men, yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I would like to look at the document again together with you, the document shown to us yesterday. This is Exhibit 1126.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this refers also to the interpreters. Your Honours, it is in our binder marked as P1037. Actually, that is Exhibit 1126. I managed to change that. E1126 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I have Exhibit 1126, but I don't have the English translation. Oh, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, you have the document in front you. I see the Prosecutor yesterday quoted the first two paragraphs from this document, and to gain time I will quote. You can look at the document, and you can also listen to what I'm saying as it is very brief. I think that will speed things up. I will quote the paragraph where it says: "In particular, we would like to draw your attention to three Arabs who, about 15 days ago, were detained at Busovaca while on route from Travnik to Split. Their names are..." then we see the three names, and then after that it says: "Please use their influence and power to secure the release of these people as soon as possible." Signed by Ahmed Adilovic. Witness, please, in connection with this document shown to you by the Prosecutor, I have the following question for you: Would you agree with me that this document does not show in any way that these men were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade? It simply mentions individuals asking for their release; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what one gathers from this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can take away the document now. I have something else to ask you now. Testifying yesterday and in answer to questions from the Prosecution, you answered that you remembered certain details regarding the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, and in that connection you mentioned that Dr. Abu Haris, with regard to the kidnapping, contacted Efendija Karalic. Do you remember that? Do you remember saying that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You emphasised that Efendija Karalic spoke Arabic so that you, yourself, did not act as interpreter between Efendija Karalic and Abu Haris; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then one could quite fairly make the conclusion that you don't know what they were talking about.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: One hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you said at a certain point in time that the exchange of Zivko Totic was not organised via Efendija Karalic or through his mediation, and then your answer was interrupted by the next question from the Prosecution, and I wish to clear this up a little. Please, you will agree with me when I say that you actually didn't know how Zivko Totic's exchange was organised, or perhaps you do know.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly. I know partly. I know some things in that connection, not everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the witness to look at document D764. For the record, until the document reaches the witness, let me say that this is a document of the European Monitoring Mission on the exchange of hostages. Actually, it is Annex B and C to their report. And I would like the witness to look at paragraph 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you please look at paragraph 5 of this document. Witness --

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that we have here an account saying that Mujahedin messengers have handed over a message to the ECMM regarding the hostages?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now look at paragraph 7 of this document. Do you agree with me that it says that the ECMM centre in Zenica contacted the Mujahedin and offered to mediate?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you now look, please, at paragraph 10 of this document, and the first two sentences only of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 2 of the English document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just the first two sentences, Mr. Awad. Do you agree that this document of the ECMM says that the 3rd Corps denies any connection with the extremists or any kind of involvement in the kidnapping? That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says in this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you now look at the next page in the English version. It is on the same page. Paragraph 12. It is a very important segment, Mr. Awad. It refers to the 7th Muslim Brigade that you testified about yesterday, so will you please read it.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it says here that the commander of the brigade denied any relationship with the extremists and asked for the whole problem of foreigners to wished to help Bosnia to be discussed?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now please also look at paragraph 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the English version be scrolled down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that it says here that the commander of the 3rd Corps claimed that the Mujahedin were not authorised to speak on behalf of the army? That is what it says here.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I have the following question for you now: You said yesterday that Dr. Abu Haris contacted Efendija Karalic, and you said that he was the emir of the brigade, and then you said that the exchange did not take place, nevertheless, through the mediation of Mr. Karalic. Doesn't this document confirm that, and what do you know about it? Is it true that the exchange was carried out through the mediation of the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. The exchange was carried out through them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit 1135, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Testifying about the events of June and July 1993, you said that you briefly stayed at the Mujahedin camp in Mehurici. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described that the Mujahedin were put up in two private homes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that when I arrived at the camp there were two houses and a path leading through a small wood, and then there was another house at the other end. So the camp consisted of these three houses altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether this perhaps was the camp in Poljanica, a small hamlet close to Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Poljanica. I have forgotten the names, but for all Arabs this whole area was known as Mehurici or, as the Arabs would put it, Mehrici [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, a few more minutes on this topic. You said that when you went to Guca Gora you visited this camp, but I have something else to ask you in that connection. In those days when you went to Guca Gora, the Mujahedin camp was not in the school in Mehurici, was it?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never mentioned the school, and I never said that the Mujahedin were in the school. I never said anything to that effect in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I know you didn't. Thank you, Mr. Awad. But I just want to make sure that this camp was in this hamlet that you described and not at the school in Mehurici. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You described your own participation in the events linked to Guca Gora. Can you recall roughly -- not roughly, but as closely as possible when that was? If you can recall.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't recollect. It was more likely that it was the second half of June. Closer to July than June itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your testimony you mentioned Bosnians who took part in that operation together with the foreign Mujahedin. They were actually local Mujahedins who joined this group of Arabs. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that on that occasion you were responsible for the wounded. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assisted. I took care of the wounded. I wasn't responsible for the wounded, but I was there to assist and take them over.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. During those combat operations you didn't see any wounded members of units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any other wounded. Only the Bosnians who were with the Mujahedin, the Arab Mujahedin, some of them were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday when testifying about this, you also mentioned that certain armed forces, military forces, should have joined this operation but they did not appear, and in that connection I want to make sure I understood you correctly. So in that operation, to the best of your knowledge, there was no participation by members of other units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this operation was actually an independent operation by a group of Mujahedin under the command of Wahiuddeen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you regarding your general knowledge about the Arabs who were present in this area from the time when you arrived and onwards. So please, when you joined the Arab fighters in April 1993, they were not a compact group, were they? I am referring to all the Arabs.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not one group. There were different people there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you're saying that there were several different groups of Arabs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were organised into groups, but I didn't see them being organised. There were several of them in different places. They were not all in one place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you specifically about the group that you joined. They were not a compact group either that remained there from April 1993 until the formation of the detachment. The group did not consist of the same people. In other words, the membership of that group changed. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abu Mali, Ejub remained, who were always there, but the others changed. There were always new faces, but number was roughly the same. Seven, eight, or ten men, never more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So some men would join the group while others would leave. So it wasn't a group of the same composition.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Local fighters would join that group, local Muslims.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this group, in Zenica. There were no local Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you the following: It would be wrong to believe that these same people of whom Wahiuddeen was the commander when you joined, that the El Mujahedin was formed of exactly the same people? That would be wrong?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a certain group who were there. Then there was others, Dr. Abu Haris, Abu Mali, Ejub, Husa Mudin [phoen]. These people that I remember, they were always there. There were people that I saw them for a while and then never again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But many of them left while others came. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Joining this group, yes. If you're referring -- or if you mean that people went out and then other people came in, well, that I couldn't say much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you is this: It would be wrong to believe, wouldn't it, that all Arabs who were active in this area before the formation of this detachment actually joined a detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So in this group of Arabs who were active in this area, there was a -- a core group that you described now which were you member of, and if I understood your testimony of yesterday, yes, correctly, you felt that it was important to organise them, and this is why you recommended that a detachment be formed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this group you mentioned as one of the group Abu Haris. Am I correct if I say that a many of these people were highly educated?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you name some of them?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, Abu Haris was a doctor. He graduated medicine in Austria, in Vienna. Muatez was a lawyer and also military personnel. I think he could have been a captain in the Egyptian army earlier. Wahiuddeen graduated from the Islamic theology school, and he had seven kirajats [phoen], and very few people actually knew seven kirajats, which means seven different ways of teaching -- or different teachings of Koran. I think Abu Mali graduated from the school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is enough. I will come back to this proposal for the establishment of a detachment. What I would like to do now is to show you the exhibit that was discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 273. For the record, let me say that this is a document from the Supreme Command Staff of 13 August 1993, and it is an order for the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment in the area of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, you mentioned the order of the supreme -- of the General Staff whereby this detachment was established. I would now like to ask you to please focus on the part which says "Mobilisation preparations." So this is the last part of the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that it says here that the replenishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment should be carried out by recruiting foreigners, volunteers? Do you agree that this is what it says?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this order was not enforced from the very beginning because local Muslims were also joining this detachment? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's about right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bosnians were continuously recruited into unit from other units, and also civilians. Local civilians were recruited into the unit regardless of this order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And irrespective of the position of the army -- of the commands of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who did not allow this movement from unit to unit. You said yesterday that they were considered to be deserters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this order that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In reference to this part of the document, I have another question. It is true, isn't it, that volunteers who joined the detachment already owned their own weapons that they acquired in different ways? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They did not receive these weapons earlier from the Bosnia and Herzegovina army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They purchased the weapons themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to seek a clarification from you. Not all Arabs who were in the area of Central Bosnia joined this detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They did not all join the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those Arabs who did not want to accept the rules of discipline which were enforced within the detachment did not join this detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it transpired from the beginning to the end. So from the time when the detachment was established through its end.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain for the Trial Chamber what the rules of discipline were in the detachment.

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say this: There was discipline within the detachment. Not everyone was free to go wherever they wanted to go, so there were orders that had to be obeyed. The emir had to be obeyed, so people had to do what the emir wanted them to do. So it was not possible to walk around -- or let me put it this way -- there were -- there was this kind of problem, for instance: Somebody wanted to get married, but then because there had already been problems there with people getting married and then getting divorced, so there was creating dissatisfaction among the population in Bosnia and Herzegovina. There was an order issued at the level of the detachment that no member of the detachment, of the El Mujahedin Detachment, was allowed to marry without the permission of the emir and unless they had already spent at least -- at least six months as members of the detachment. And only once they were issued this permission to marry were they allowed to marry. This was done so the problems that appeared in the field that were assigned -- or attributed to the Mujahedin would be removed. Bosniaks considered every Arab who came to -- everyone who came to Bosnia and Herzegovina who wore a uniform and wore a beard, they considered them Mujahedin, to be Mujahedin. And even some people who worked for humanitarian organisations, the people in Bosnia referred to them as El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I would just like to clarify this a bit more. In other words, am I correct, have I understood you correctly, that what you're saying is that the people in Central Bosnia considered every Arab who wore a beard and a uniform a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment? Is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, let us elaborate on this a bit longer. Would it be correct to say that at this time and in this area there were several different groups of Asian and African background active in the area, not only the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that. There were other Arabs who were not members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall who these people would be? Can you recall what the groups were or categories of people?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall this because I didn't have many contacts with these people, so I didn't know many details about them, but there were some people who felt that they should in no way fight side by side with the Bosnian army. They had their own views, and for them this army was not Islamic enough. In other words, they were not allowed by Islam to fight in an army of this type, so they did not want to join the BH army. They even considered us renegades from the -- from the faith because we were part of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we just clarify something here? The people that you mentioned now who were there and who lived and were active in Central Bosnia during this period, the same period, they, too, participated in combat activities in their own way and on their own; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. There wasn't enough information, but from what I understood, they, too, fought there, but they were not part of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they were not part of the El Mujahedin Detachment either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And that we were considered to be renegades from the faith. In other words, that we were not Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And with which army did these people fight? I'm not saying against which army, I'm saying with. If they regarded you as renegades for fighting side by side with the ABiH, which army did they fight side by side with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Do you know if they coordinated their actions with the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that information. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, I didn't quite understand. You said that you were not viewed well because you were fighting within the army or with the army. In the army or with the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that we formed, established a detachment which was part of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm a little confused. In war, or in the war that was taking place in Central Bosnia at the time, there were two parties to the war. It was the Muslim -- the ABiH against the -- the Serbian armies isn't it so? Right. Now, these --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- these Arabs who regarded you as the renegades for supporting the ABiH, do you know whether they were fighting on the side of the Serbs against the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Heaven forbid. They wouldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But now my problem is if they didn't do that and they were not fighting on the side of the ABiH, on whose side were they fighting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will explain that in a minute so that you can understand me, but please listen carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please. That's -- that was my original question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned to you that when I came to Bosnia and Herzegovina I came because I was a believer and I wanted to help Muslims. And there were other Muslims who came to Bosnia and Herzegovina for the same reasons, because they were Muslims and because they wanted to help the people, the Bosnian people. However, not all these people who came from elsewhere, Muslims -- they did not have the same understanding of Islam. Some of them considered that because the state, the Bosnian and Herzegovinian state, said that they would be a secular state, they considered this state to be a state that they should not assist in any manner. And because the army of this state, the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that would be that that army, too, was secular, so -- because if there were no Islamic elements within that army, they should not join and fight with that army. So what they did is they would go to a certain area, spend their seven days. Because as I said a little earlier, the people in the field, they saw all these people as El Mujahedin. So they would call them El Mujahedin even if they were not members of the detachment. So the Bosnian people, in other words, they saw every Arab -- and even I when I came there originally, when I was a member of a humanitarian organisation, I was considered a Mujahedin. In other words, the -- the people would consider -- as soon as they saw an Arab, they would consider them Mujahedin. They were brave, courageous, and so on. So this is something that I myself had occasion to experience. I would, say, walk into an establishment, and then people would say, "Please come in," welcome me there. So there were people who would just go to the front line without asking anyone. The army would accept them there, the -- the troops in the field. They would stay there for a couple of days, seven days, fight with them. So I wouldn't really say whether they fought with the army. This was really their own decision. I don't know if you understand what I'm trying to tell you. This is all I can say. I was trying to explain it so that you get a better feel for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're confusing me even more. My problem is here are two groups of Islam. The one group has decided that they are going to help the ABiH in its war. Okay? The other group says, "We don't want to help you because you're a secular state, and we regard these Arabs who are with you as renegades." Now, when they go to the battlefield for seven days, on whose side are they fighting if they don't want to support this secular army and they can't find -- they don't want to fight on the side of the Serbs? Who are they -- on whose were they fighting? That -- I just want that answer. Don't tell me about -- that long explanation didn't answer my question. Just tell me, "They were fighting on so-and-so's side," or, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said earlier that they wanted to help the Bosniak Muslims. They did not want to be part of the official authorities or the official army that they considered to be secular. They wanted to give their participation in any other way. Did you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another question. Did they receive orders from any foreign organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't understand. Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These people who were not fighting, the Mujahedin who were not fighting within the army and within the detachment, were they fighting, receiving orders from abroad, from any foreign organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't say that, no, because they came -- let me explain. The Mujahedin who came to Bosnia and Herzegovina didn't come in an organised manner. They were not sent by any side. No one sent them as a state or an organisation: "You go to Bosnia and fight there." People felt that something awoke in them when they saw what was happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they felt obliged to help. You understand that's why they came without any organisation. And I don't believe that anyone from the outside could order those people. Maybe they had financial links with someone, but as for orders and fighting, I would not say that, definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, I'm going to now put something to you as a follow-up to a question by Her Honour Judge Lattanzi. Would you agree with the following: You actually personally did not know all the people or groups of people who came to Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't have the opportunity to speak with those people either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you really cannot know why any of those groups or any of those people had actually come to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Would you accept that? You cannot know that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking generally. People had come with that general intention of fighting, of helping. I cannot say that applied to all of them. Maybe some did not come with that intention.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is precisely the point. Would you agree with me that you can speak here about what you know or what you heard from other people? That is something that you do know. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask you this: Before forming the El Mujahedin Detachment, there was a differentiation in the group of Arabs at Mehurici, and some of them had already split off from this main group where you were and Dr. Abu Haris and Abu Mali, in May 1993, or at that time approximately. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people had left. Let's go back a little bit. Earlier you showed a document where there were the names of three people who had been captured by the Croats. Before me, they tried to leave Bosnia and Herzegovina because they did not like -- they didn't like the organisation and the fighting and all of the things that were happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Perhaps they regretted being there, and they tried to return and were captured on their way out. So you can say that there was a splitting off, and some people left that group that was in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that some of them stayed in Bosnia and Herzegovina and were active in fighting unconnected to this group of Arabs connected to Dr. Abu Haris? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, different individuals and groups, for example Abu Dzafer, Ali Ahmed Al Hamad [phoen] had their own groups, but they never became members of the detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The detachment itself was left by some problematic people who had remained in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and continued to fight on their own in their own way. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Not only your group under Dr. Abu Haris considered themselves as Mujahedin. Others also -- other Arabs considered themselves as Mujahedin, ones that had come to Bosnia and fought without being connected to the detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No could take away from them their right to call themselves Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that many incidents committed by those people were ascribed to the El Mujahedin Detachment or to the group around Abu Hasan [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Abu Haris," interpreter's correction. Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Awad, the interpreters would like you to please repeat your answer. They didn't hear you very well, so start last answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said yes, that is correct. The problems that they created is something that still gives me a headache up to this day. It's something that is ascribed to me. Whenever I speak with someone, journalists or someone, they say, "Your people did this, this, and this." No. My people did not do that. Do you understand me? And that is why I still have headaches because of those problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Awad, many incidents committed by Arabs who were not in the detachment were ascribed to the El Mujahedin Detachment. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I can even tell you about an instance, and it's something that makes a person have a hard time about it. On one occasion somebody stole a vehicle, a jeep. I think this happened in 1995. Somebody stole some jeep. Some Arab person did this, and the 3rd Corps military security sent a man to the El Mujahedin command, and we were charged with the theft of this jeep. I took this person to our garage. I showed him how many jeeps we had that we had purchased with our own money. I even reminded him that we as a detachment, as a group of people, gave to the 3rd Corps such an all-terrain vehicle as a present. We did not need to steal. Everything that happened was ascribed to the El Mujahedin Detachment, and then they would come to our doors to ask, "What did your members do?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We will certainly get back to these incidents that were committed by foreigners who were not members of the EMD, but you have mentioned one example now, a theft of a car, but what other incidents are we talking about? What was the nature of the actions committed by these other groups that were so terrible that you didn't want to have anything to do with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will give you an example. Ninety-third is constantly being preferred to, the slapping of girls in Zenica who were walking around in miniskirts, or bathed by the river, or when they were caught like a couple when was -- when a couple was caught that was going around holding hands or kissing on the streets, that they were getting slapped, and it was automatically said that this was done by members of the El Mujahedin Detachment. I say that this was not done by members of El Mujahedin Detachment, definitely, but this was done by people who wanted to tarnish the reputation of the El Mujahedin Detachment, and that's why I say I had headaches all the time from this. And when people talk about these problems, they speak about them with conviction. They don't ask if this happened, but they say that members of the El Mujahedin Detachment did this, this, and this without checking the information. We're charged right at the beginning. If they said, "Some Arab did this," I would accept that, because when an incident or a problem occurs, each perpetrator of that incident has a name, a first and a last name, is not carrying the name or bearing the name of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you understand what I'm trying to say now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 841.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's a document of the 3rd Corps Military Security Service, dated the 5th of November, 1995. It's headed "Information," and it's sent to the 7th Corps Military Security Service. It's a small document, a short document. I believe that you will read it quickly. The document refers to the incident in which members of the El Mujahedin Unit allegedly took place -- took part, led by Abu Hamza, and then it continues to say that the command of the El Mujahedin Detachment informed that Abu Hamza is not a member of their unit. And I would like to ask you the following, please, Mr. Awad: You know who Abu Hamza is, who had a group at Guca Gora; is that correct? Is that correct? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that man a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment. He was thrown out of the El Mujahedin Detachment. For a while, by mistake, he was still kept on the list, I think, but he was thrown out of the El Mujahedin Detachment and erased from the register. He did not obey anyone. He was off by himself. He had a couple of supports with him. That man that -- even after the war created problems, and he's now in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Awad, I want to ask you this: During 1993, he had a group. Before the detachment was formed, he had a group at Guca Gora which was is not under the command of Dr. Abu Haris; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a certain number of people who did not wish to be under the command of Dr. Abu Haris.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you remember when he was thrown out of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact date. I was not in the personnel department, so I don't know that, but I know that it was said that he had been thrown out of the detachment, that he was not a member of the detachment. I know that that's what was said, that he was thrown out. I don't have the exact record of the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How about the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot remember. I don't even want to say anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify this: When we're talking about Abu Hamza and his actions at Guca Gora, I want it to be clear that I was talking about the period before the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment when I asked you about him being -- not being under the command of Dr. Abu Haris. Is that how you understood my question?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him before. I did not meet him earlier, so I cannot say since I did not see him. I know that he was at Guca Gora, that he was there, so it's probably like that in that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Like this: Do you agree would me that you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was just going to say that the exhibit that you have just shown to the witness is dated the 5th of November, 1995, and it is replying to a document that was sent on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have finished with this document. It is already an exhibit, and these questions are no longer related to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. All I'm saying is the complaint about Abu Hamza is around November 1995, not 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, quite correct. That is one group of questions. But my last question that I now wish to complete and to clear up with the witness is as follows:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this was a document there 1995. You realise that, don't you? But something else that I asked you is -- I went back to the period prior to the establishment of the detachment in 1993 and to the area of Guca Gora, and with respect to Abu Hamza, my question was, was he under the command of Abu Haris, and your answer was that you didn't see him. Do you agree with me that Abu Haris's group, before the establishment of the detachment, was a small group of people?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was located in Poljance, I think. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On condition that he was in that group of people at that time, would you have known him? Would you have come across him because you were a member of that group?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly should have seen him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now wish the witness to be shown an excerpt from Exhibit 92, the page with the number 04717277.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see you smiling. You obviously know that person; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell me, please, the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Imad Al-Hussein, or so-called Abu Hamza, but not that Abu Hamza.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Imad Al-Hussein, Abu Hamza, is not the person from Guca Gora that we have been talking about, and he is not the person that caused incident; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a great friend of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the nickname Abu Hamza is quite a frequent nickname?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People like to give the name Hamza. I'll explain how. The name Hamza is the name of a messenger who was killed, and he's considered a champion martyr, shaheed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for having to interrupt you sometimes, because I have so many questions for you. I now wish to ask you about another person. Have you heard of a person called Abu Zubeir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in Central Bosnia, in the period from the spring of 1993 until the end of the war, there were several persons in that area with the same nickname, Abu Zubeir?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were from Tunisia, from Saudi Arabia, from Yemen, from various countries, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The person Abu Zubeir Al Hayili from Saudi Arabia was a person who in several places in Bosnia and Herzegovina had his groups from the spring of 1993 until the end of the war. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: AJMAN AWAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
